_comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the fakefish playback/session constants.
Edit ONLY this file, then run `uv run fakefish-gen-constants`. That regenerates BOTH
firmware/eel_core/stim_levels.h   (C, consumed by the sketches)
src/fakefish/_constants.py        (Python, consumed by the toolchain)
and the CI gate asserts the regeneration leaves no git diff. Never hand-edit either
generated file — your edit will be silently reverted by the next codegen run.
NOT here on purpose:
* the SAMPLE RATE. It stays single-sourced in the export-generated eel_stimuli.h
(STIM_SAMPLE_RATE_HZ) / export_teensy_stimuli.PLAYBACK_RATE_HZ; the generated files
derive every sample-unit figure FROM it rather than restating it.
* StimKind. Already single-sourced in the export tool, which defines the Python STIM_*
values and emits the matching C enum.
* pins, thresholds, debounce, calibration. Those are per-surface (L3) or per-board (L1)
and live in firmware/eel_core/config.h or the sketch's own control header.
BOTH DEVICES NOW MARK WITH EEL PULSES, BUT WITH DIFFERENT CODES. NOT UNIFIED.
sd_path.pulse_marker = 6 EOD pulses at a fixed 10 Hz with ALTERNATING polarity,
baked into the WAVs by build_sd_card.py. Identifies a playback.
Emitted as SD_MARKER_*.
rc_path.pulse_marker = 2 or 4 EOD pulses at a fixed 100 Hz, SAME polarity, synthesised
live by the RC device. The COUNT tags volley vs sham.
Emitted as PULSE_MARKER_*.
The distinct prefixes are deliberate: a bare MARKER_* name in a repo with two marker
codes is a trap.
(History: the SD device used a 10 kHz SINE tone until 2026-08-17. It was removed because
the per-channel 2-pole output filter attenuates 10 kHz by ~21.8 dB, and because everything
the device emits should be made of eel pulses. See TODO.md.)
Consumed today by build_sd_card.py (Python), which BAKES these into the WAV card.
Also emitted to C as SD_* for a future live surface that renders these on-device.
Absolute output levels as a fraction of full scale (baked into the WAVs, NOT
peak-normalised).
LOCALIZATION IS A QUARTER OF THE VOLLEY, NOT A HALF (changed 2026-08-21, with the
fitted volley model). The synthetic volleys now carry the MEASURED within-volley
amplitude envelope, which decays ~22 % across a volley at the median and reaches
~0.34 of the volley's own peak at the 5th percentile. At the old 2:1 ratio the tail
of a decaying volley landed on top of the localization level, which is exactly the
separation that ratio existed to provide. Dropping localization to 1/4 restores it
without clipping the envelope: the retired alternative was a VOLLEY_DECAY_FLOOR
that flattened the measured decay on 64 % of volleys.
The absolute step between a volley and a resting discharge is NOT a measurement --
docs/VOLLEY_GENERATIVE_SPEC.md section 5 is explicit that it is confounded by
distance and clipping and must be treated as a knob. This is that knob.
The lead-in that identifies a playback: n_pulses EOD pulses at a FIXED rate with
ALTERNATING polarity, prepended to every B/C/D session.
Why this is detectable, and why each parameter is what it is:
* ALTERNATING polarity is the discriminator. No real eel alternates, and a
localization train is single-polarity, so the pattern cannot be confused with
biology or with the stimulus that follows it.
* Alternation also SURVIVES the firmware's per-press random polarity flip: the flip
negates the whole WAV, so the absolute sign is unpredictable but the alternation
is invariant. Detect the pattern, never the sign.
* n_pulses must be EVEN so the burst is CHARGE-BALANCED (equal numbers of each
polarity of an identical waveform => net charge ~0). This replaces the zero-sum
property the old sine LUT provided. The codegen asserts it.
* rate_hz sits BELOW the volley range (which peaks at 300-400 Hz) and the IPI stays
far longer than one EOD, so marker pulses never overlap.
Provisional values, easy to retune here: 6 pulses at 10 Hz.
Program A: a steady, single-polarity EOD train at a known rate and level — a plain
reference signal for setting gain and checking the rig. Single-polarity (unlike the
marker) so it is unambiguously a calibration signal and not a lead-in code; its net
charge is balanced across presses by the firmware's random polarity flip, exactly as
for the localization program.

session._comment: Session structure. Seconds/ms here; sample units are derived at codegen from the sample rate.

_comment: Consumed today by the RC sketch (C). NOMINAL levels only — on the 36 V DRV8871 stage
amplitude 1.0 means the full rail, so these are rail fractions, not volts.
Coded preamble: a short EOD burst at a fixed IPI, tagged by PULSE COUNT — a volley is
pulses_volley pulses then the discharge, a sham is pulses_sham pulses then silence.
ipi_samp 500 @ 50 kHz = 10 ms = 100 Hz: clearly above localization (<=20 Hz) and below
the volley peak (~300-400 Hz). max_pulses sizes the static marker IPI table.
BLINDED TRIALS. The RC trigger fires in ONE direction only, and the firmware draws
volley-vs-sham itself at the moment of playback. The operator throws 'fire a trial'
and cannot choose which they deliver, so when and where they fire cannot correlate
with the trial type — that correlation is the bias this removes.
p_volley is the probability the draw yields a VOLLEY (the rest are shams). 0.5 is a
balanced design; raise it to spend fewer trials on controls.
The draw happens in the sample-clock ISR, NOT in loop(), because random() is called
from the ISR elsewhere (polarity, localization jitter) and must stay single-caller.
Note this blinds the CHOICE, not the outcome: the LED still shows a distinct sham
pattern afterwards, and the recording still tells the two apart by marker pulse
count (which analysis needs).
The amplitude control sets the VOLLEY (max); localization is DERIVED as volley /
volley_amp_ratio (a quarter at 4.0). Anchoring at the volley keeps the ratio at every
pot position and needs no clamp. panel_volley_amp is the bench default with no transmitter.
4.0, not 2.0, since 2026-08-21: the synthetic volleys carry the measured amplitude
envelope, whose tail reaches ~0.34 of the volley's peak. At 2:1 that tail sat at the
localization level. Mirrors sd_path.levels.loc -- see the note there for the full
reasoning. The pedestal (OUT_PEDESTAL_DUTY) is what makes a quarter-scale pulse still
leave the driver dead zone cleanly.
Live localization train. Since 2026-08-21 its RHYTHM comes from a model fitted to
99 010 measured resting intervals (data/loc_model_params.json, vendored; see
docs/LOCALIZATION_GENERATIVE_SPEC.md and firmware/eel_core/loc_rhythm.h), not from
the unit-mean lognormal draw it used before. The model's own tables are NOT here --
they are generated into firmware/eel_core/loc_model_params.h from that JSON. Only
the KNOB RANGES the operator sees live here.
min_hz / max_hz are the CH3 throttle's ladder, and they are now a TICK TEMPO -- one
over the median interval, the number quoted as an eel's discharge rate -- because the
device anchors the median rather than the mean. The measured eel ticks at 3.15 Hz
(LOC_NOMINAL_TICK_HZ), with real single-fish slices spanning roughly 1.3-9.7 Hz, so
the 1-20 Hz ladder still brackets real behaviour at both ends.
This is the change of meaning to watch: under the retired lognormal, a setting of
5 Hz meant 5 pulses per second on AVERAGE. It now means the fish ticks at 5 Hz, which
at panel_randomness 1.0 delivers about 3.3 pulses/s -- the interval distribution is
heavy-tailed, and one long silence eats half the average while contributing one
interval to the median. Spec section 5.3 has the full argument; knobs.gain_mean_anchor
in the model JSON is the table that would restore the old meaning.
panel_randomness is the bench default for CH5 (was panel_cv, a coefficient of
variation). 1.0 IS the measured eel: 0 is a metronome at the nominal tempo and the
knob is useful to about 1.5. It is not a jitter amount and does not blend toward a
Poisson process -- the lag-1 autocorrelation stays around 0.52 across the whole range.
refractory_samp is the minimum IPI (5 ms @ 50 kHz); it MUST stay greater than
EOD_HV_LEN so localization pulses can never overlap -- that is what lets locgen use a
single-pulse scheduler instead of the overlap-add engine. It is now a pure safety
floor: the model's fastest possible interval is 27.9 ms (1394 samples) at tempo 1, so
it only engages if the rate knob is driven far past any real eel.
